thread.title: Intel Broadens Product Lineup With 5G Baseband Chips | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Intel Broadens Product Lineup With 5G Baseband Chips | Investor's Business Daily
text:
LAS VEGAS — PC and server chip giant Intel ( INTC ) plans to aggressively expand into other markets including chips for wireless communications, artificial intelligence and autonomous driving.
X
That was the main message at the chipmaker's media briefing Monday on the eve of CES 2019 , the massive annual consumer electronics show.
Intel already is taking on wireless chip leader Qualcomm ( QCOM ) in the smartphone modem market and plans to come out with a 5G wireless chip in the second half of the year. Apple ( AAPL ) is the primary customer for that chip.
During the same time frame, Intel also intends to sell chips for 5G base stations. These provide technology for cellular towers to process calls and data. Those base station chips are code-named Snow Ridge.
 "We're excited about Snow Ridge," said Navin Shenoy, executive vice president of Intel's Data Center Group. "It will take our position in the base station market from zero percent just a few years ago to what we predict will be over 40% by the year 2022."
Qualcomm Claims Crown Earlier Monday, rival Qualcomm touted its leadership position in 5G wireless technology at its own media event ahead of CES.
Intel on Monday announced six new ninth-generation Core desktop personal computer chips using 10-nanometer process technology. It plans to release new mobile PC processors in the second quarter.
The company also showcased its latest Xeon Scalable data-center products, which feature advanced AI and memory capabilities.
All told, Intel is pursuing a total addressable market for semiconductors worth $300 billion, the largest in the company's history.
Intel stock gained a fraction to close at 47.74 on the stock market today .
